beats.text: The Supreme Court ruled that Tesla invented radio.
beats.note: A 1984 New York Times article said the Justices overturned Marconi's patent because Tesla's work came first, according to Mercurians, which calls such accounts inaccurate.
Marconi sued in the Court of Claims over four US patents. Chief Justice Stone wrote the opinion.
The Court held that Stone's patent anticipated Marconi's, and that Marconi's patent disclosed no invention over it.

beats.text: One piece of the prior art.
beats.note: Tesla's patent disclosed a four circuit system but lacked a variable inductance for tuning. The Court said Lodge supplied it.

beats.text: Marconi's original patent was not in question.
beats.note: The Court said his reputation as the first to achieve successful radio transmission rests on that original patent.

beats.text: Nobody ruled on who invented radio.
beats.note: Mercurians says the Supreme Court never determined that Tesla invented radio. The ruling was about the validity of Marconi's later claims.

beats.text: Tesla's name is in the ruling as prior art. Not as the winner.
